Hey everyone, I’ve been thinking about taking on the No-the Spectral Cutlass Challenge on iOS, and I wanted to get a feel for whether it’s actually doable or just a nightmare. For those who don’t know, this challenge requires you to complete the whole Greenwater Bay region without ever using the Spectral Cutlass, which is honestly the go-to weapon for most players because of its speed and damage. On mobile, the controls can be a bit fiddly, so I’m wondering if skipping it just makes the run too slow or tedious.

Has anyone tried a no-cutlass run recently? I’m curious about tips on alternative weapons or strategies that can help shave off time. I figure the other swords or maybe even the unique upgraded bows might help, but I’m worried the lack of quick close-range attacks will bottleneck the run, especially on some of the timed escort and stealth sections. Also, managing the inventory and quick switching on iOS feels clunky compared to other platforms, so any advice on how to optimize loadouts would be awesome.

If anyone has videos or personal experiences with this challenge, please share! I want to know if this is a cool new speedrun niche or just grinding through Greenwater Bay’s hardest parts without the Spectral Cutlass is a nightmare that only a masochist would attempt. Thanks!

Hey! I’ve actually tried the Spectral Cutlass challenge a few times on iOS, and while it’s definitely tough, I do think it’s feasible with some solid practice and the right setup. The biggest hurdle for me was always that tight window to dodge those shadow wraiths right after the second phase—timing has to be near perfect. On the plus side, the touchscreen controls feel surprisingly smooth once you get used to swiping instead of button mashing.

One thing that really made a difference was focusing on upgrading your agility early on. It might seem like a stretch since you want raw damage, but the extra dodge frames give you a little breathing room in those chaotic moments. Also, using the quickstrike combo helps shave off valuable seconds, which is crucial if you’re aiming for a sub-7 minute run. If you can manage your stamina carefully, you can keep pressure consistently and minimize those risky moments.

I’d say if you’re serious about nailing it, watching some of the top runners’ clips definitely helps. They have some super tight inputs and decision-making that’s way beyond casual play. But with patience and focused practice, I think anyone dedicated enough can pull it off on iOS. Definitely worth the grind if you want a challenge that really tests your reflexes and strategy!

Hey! I gave the No-the spectral cutlass challenge a shot last week on my iPhone, and honestly, it’s tough but doable if you’re super precise. The biggest hurdle, at least for me, was timing the parry perfectly to avoid the energy drain penalty — that little window feels razor-thin on the touch controls. I found that practicing the rhythm on the first two stages before the actual cutlass fight made a huge difference.

One thing that helped was turning off all notifications and playing in airplane mode to avoid any lag spikes or accidental taps. Also, watch your stamina bar like a hawk because the spectral cutlass fight punishes you hard if you overextend. I wouldn’t call it casual-play friendly, but if you’re into optimizing each movement and willing to grind the timing, you can nail it in under 4 minutes.

There’s a sweet spot with the dodge animations, too — I figured out that canceling the dodge slightly early lets you reposition faster, which is pivotal when the cutlass swings get unpredictable. Honestly, I’m curious if anyone’s managed to do it without using the “focus shard” boost? It feels like an extra crutch but could be the key to a sub-3:30 run. Would love to hear if you’ve found consistent setups or any cool tricks!

Oh, the Spectral Cutlass challenge on No-the? I’ve toyed around with it a bit, and I’d say it’s definitely feasible, but it’s not exactly a walk in the park. The key is mastering the timing for the spectral strikes—if you can get those window attacks down tight, you can chain combos way faster than it seems at first glance. I found that locking in on the mid-range enemies first helps you dodge the tougher mobs later on with fewer hiccups.

One trick I picked up was to use the environment to your advantage, especially in those narrow corridors where enemies tend to stack up. It feels a bit counterintuitive because it limits movement, but controlling enemy flow makes managing the spectral slashes way easier. Just be wary of the shadow assassins that spawn unexpectedly—they’ll ruin your rhythm if you’re not constantly aware of your surroundings.

If you’re running this on iOS, minimizing distractions can be a huge help too, since even a slight lag can throw off your timing. Personally, I use earphones to catch all the subtle audio cues that signal enemy attacks and spectral charge-ups. Overall, it’s a tough challenge but absolutely doable with consistent practice and the right strategy. Keep at it!
